verses.text: Abraham was old, well along in years, and Yahweh had blessed him in every way.
Abraham said to the senior servant in his household, who managed everything he owned, "Put your hand under my thigh.
I want you to swear by Yahweh, the God of heaven and earth, that you won't get a wife for my son from the Canaanite women among whom I live.
Instead, go to my homeland, to my relatives, and find a wife for my son Isaac."
The servant asked him, "What if the woman won't come with me to this land? Should I take your son back to the land you came from?"
Abraham replied, "Make sure you don't take my son back there.

Yahweh, the God of heaven, brought me away from my father's household and the land where I was born. He spoke to me and swore, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' He will send his angel ahead of you, and you'll find a wife for my son there.
If the woman won't come with you, then you'll be released from this oath to me. But don't take my son back there."
So the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore to carry out this promise.
The servant took ten of his master's camels and loaded them with all kinds of valuable gifts from his master. He set out for Mesopotamia, for the city of Nahor.
He made the camels kneel outside the city beside a well. It was evening, when the women came out to draw water.
He prayed, "Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please make this journey succeed today. Show your kindness to my master Abraham.
I'm standing here by the spring, and the young women of the city are coming out to draw water.

Let the young woman I ask, 'Please lower your jar so I can drink,' be the one who answers, 'Drink, and I'll give your camels water too.' Let that be the woman you've chosen for your servant Isaac. That's how I'll know you've shown kindness to my master."
Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her water jar on her shoulder. She was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor.
The young woman was very beautiful, a virgin whom no man had known. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came back up.
The servant hurried to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water from your jar."
She said, "Drink, my lord," and quickly lowered her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink.
When she had finished giving him water, she said, "I'll draw water for your camels too, until they're done drinking."
She quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well, and drew water for all his camels.
The man watched her closely and stayed quiet, trying to learn whether Yahweh had made his journey succeed.
When the camels finished drinking, the man took a gold ring weighing half a shekel and two gold bracelets weighing ten shekels.
He asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room at your father's house for us to stay tonight?"
She answered, "I'm Bethuel's daughter. Milcah bore him to Nahor."
She added, "We have plenty of straw and feed, and there's room for you to stay."
The man bowed his head and worshiped Yahweh.
He said, "Blessed be Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham. He hasn't withheld his kindness and faithfulness from my master. Yahweh has led me straight to my master's relatives."
The young woman ran home and told her mother's household what had happened.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban. Laban ran out to the man at the spring.
He had seen the ring and bracelets on his sister's hands, and heard Rebekah tell what the man had said. So he went out and found the man standing by his camels at the spring.
Laban said, "Come in, you who are blessed by Yahweh. Why are you standing out here? I've prepared the house and a place for the camels."
The man came into the house, and the camels were unloaded. Laban provided straw and feed for them, and water for the man and his companions to wash their feet.
Food was put before him, but he said, "I won't eat until I've told you why I came." Laban said, "Go ahead."
He said, "I'm Abraham's servant.
Yahweh has greatly blessed my master, and he's become wealthy. Yahweh has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels, and donkeys.
Sarah, my master's wife, gave birth to a son for him in her old age. My master has given everything he owns to that son.
My master made me swear this: 'Don't get a wife for my son from the Canaanite women in whose land I live.
Go instead to my father's household and my relatives, and get a wife for my son.'
I asked my master, 'What if the woman won't come with me?'
He answered, 'Yahweh, whom I follow, will send his angel with you and make your journey succeed. Get a wife for my son from my relatives, from my father's household.
Then you'll be released from my oath if you go to my relatives and they refuse to give her to you.'
Today I came to the spring and prayed, 'Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please make this journey succeed.
I'm standing beside this spring. When a young woman comes out to draw water, I'll ask her, "Please give me a little water from your jar.
If she answers, "Drink, and I'll draw water for your camels too," then let her be the woman Yahweh has chosen for my master's son.'
Before I had finished praying silently, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. I said, 'Please give me a drink.'
She quickly lowered her jar and said, 'Drink, and I'll give your camels water too.' I drank, and she watered the camels as well.
I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'Bethuel's daughter; Milcah bore him to Nahor.' Then I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her hands.
I bowed my head, worshiped Yahweh, and blessed Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to get my master's brother's daughter for his son.
Now tell me whether you'll show my master kindness and faithfulness. If not, tell me, so I can decide where to go next."
Laban and Bethuel answered, "This comes from Yahweh. We can't say yes or no.
Rebekah is here with you. Take her and go. Let her become your master's son's wife, as Yahweh has spoken."
When Abraham's servant heard their answer, he bowed to the ground before Yahweh.
He brought out silver and gold jewelry and clothing and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave valuable gifts to her brother and mother.
Then he and his companions ate and drank and stayed the night. In the morning he said, "Send me back to my master."
Her brother and mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us for a few days, at least ten. Then she can go."
But he said, "Don't hold me back. Yahweh has made my journey succeed. Send me on my way to my master."
They said, "Let's call the young woman and ask her."
They called Rebekah and asked, "Will you go with this man?" She said, "I will go."
So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way with her nurse, along with Abraham's servant and his men.
They blessed Rebekah and said, "Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your descendants take possession of the cities of those who hate them."
Rebekah and her attendants got up, mounted the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah with him and left.
Isaac had come from the direction of Beer-lahai-roi; he was living in the Negev.
One evening Isaac went out into the field to meditate. He looked up and saw camels approaching.
Rebekah looked up too. When she saw Isaac, she got down from her camel.
She asked the servant, "Who is that man walking across the field to meet us?" He said, "That's my master." So she took her veil and covered herself.
The servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of his mother Sarah. He married her, and she became his wife. He loved her, and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
